issue.title: waits-lane fs trigger globs month shards, so done.json/waiting.json writes never fire wait_checks or bead_claim_checks

task_type_fields.impact:
`wait_checks` is effectively a 120 s-backstop job, so about 82% of October dependency
waits were released by the parked runner's 60 s fallback. Measured release latency is
p50 ~21–33 s, p90 ~58 s after the dependency session finished, against an advertised
10 s lane. Every fallback pass is also a ~5 s full project index build per parked runner
per minute.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/default_config.yml waits routine (wait_checks, bead_claim_checks fs trigger glob */artifacts/ace-run/*); src/sase/axe/chop_policy_snapshots.py:_fs_watch_token
task_type_fields.repro:
The shipped `waits` routine gives `wait_checks` and `bead_claim_checks` an `fs` trigger on
`{path: projects, glob: "*/artifacts/ace-run/*"}` with `max_quiet: "120s"`
(`src/sase/default_config.yml:1326-1376`). `_fs_watch_token`
(`src/sase/axe/chop_policy_snapshots.py`) records only a shallow
`name:mtime:size:child_count` per glob match. Canonical runs are day-sharded
(`ace-run/YYYYMM/DD/<timestamp>/`), so the glob matches **month shards** (plus hidden lock
files), and `done.json` / `waiting.json` writes never change the token.

Reproduce on athena (2026-10-07):

1. `stat -c '%n %y' ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifacts/ace-run/202610 ~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifacts/ace-run/202610/07`
   gives month 00:13:32 vs day 13:37:33. Runs completing all day never move the watched mtime.
2. Of the 11 newest `~/.sase/axe/lumberjacks/waits/chops/wait_checks/runs/*.json`, 8 were
   `skipped: watched paths unchanged and within max_quiet`.
3. The glob matches 2,365 entries, of which at least 2,334 are hidden
   `..monitor-start-*`, `..gate-shell-*`, and `..gate-turn-*` lock files. The job therefore
   fires only on `max_quiet` or incidental lock churn.
4. October runner logs (`~/.sase/workflows/202610/*.txt`): 304 dependency waits were
   released by "runner fallback (ready.json not observed)" vs 68 via `ready.json`.

`tests/test_axe_default_chop_triggers.py` hides the bug by creating the run directory
directly under the month shard. `docs/axe.md` still says an idle tick re-scans "when a
project gains a new agent artifact".

Suggested fix (research recommendation, Phase 1 step 2):

- Add `{path: projects, glob: "*/artifacts/.ace_refresh_pulse"}` to both triggers.
  `write_done_marker_and_update_index` already touches that pulse.
- Make `write_waiting_marker` touch it too.
- Drop or narrow the `ace-run/*` entry.
- Fix the test fixture to use the real `YYYYMM/DD/<run>` layout, and fix the docs.

Do not deepen the glob: that would stat all of history every tick.

issue.creation_reason: Found while consolidating research.40 on jobs vs service procs: this blind trigger is the main reason waiting agents wake slowly, and fixing it is the cheapest lever.

payload.description: Both slow wait_checks: the blind trigger delays when it runs, and the dead-waiter scan makes each run ~29s; a fast pulse-driven cadence needs both fixed

payload.entry: Verified by sase-1hf.land on master 3a4178b15a: wait_checks (now in the agent_waits routine) and bead_claim_checks watch {path: projects, glob: '*/artifacts/.ace_refresh_pulse'} with max_quiet 120s; write_waiting_marker and the TUI wait editor touch the project pulse for dependency-carrying markers only; trigger tests use the real ace-run/YYYYMM/DD/<run> layout; docs/axe.md describes the pulse. The done.json writer audit is recorded on sase-1hf.2 note #1.

payload.close_reason: Fixed by epic sase-1hf phases sase-1hf.2 (pulse-trigger, ea7d1388db) and sase-1hf.5 (lane-split, 3a4178b15a)
